title: Working in his father's rice business and the fishing supply store
summary: After quitting music he sold rice, later joining the Decatur Street fisherman supply business his family has run since 1800.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: When you quit playing, what did you do?
Oh, I didn't, I just went to dances, Dick. I used to like to.
I mean, you worked though, huh?
Oh yeah, I was working for my father in the rice business. He had the Ciccola rice mill. And I was selling clean rice to the grocery trade in and around New Orleans, you know.
Rice, yeah. My dad was a miller. Uh-huh.
How'd you happen to get in this business?
My brother got in this business with Joe Sycaluca about 30 years ago, and about 22 years ago, I come with him here. After Joe died, I come in this business with him.
That's in Sydney? Sydney, yeah. Well, your family's been on Decatur Street a long time, huh?

Since 1800, yeah. Yeah, my great-grandfather before my dad was in Caughty and Decatur. He was in general merchandise store, similar to this. Those days, those kind of people sold, stores sold groceries and all kind of supplies, plantation supplies. Well, a person coming from the country wanted to make one stop. He might even ask you to buy him three dozen diapers or something. I've had them ask me that. Uh-huh. Where they could, could I get them a couple of dozen diapers? Yeah, yeah. Because we got a varied line here, man. We got a heck of a lot of items in this place. You don't realize it until you walk through it and see what's in it. I got a man there with me three years, and he don't know the stock here. And he's a pretty bright fella, that fella had it. And he's here last September pass for three years. You just can't learn stuff.
Well, it's not, it's not that, Dick. It's a, it's a tough business to learn. It's, it's netting here. Uh-huh. It's a business in itself.

Learning the sizes and the, the, the sizes of the mesh and what each is used for. Taught to speak intelligently to people. There's linen weapon, that stuff is $4.95 a pound. You, you don't leave your errors to make any mistakes. You can't make no mistakes with it. Uh-huh. You know what I mean, Paul? There's my own prime, $2.75 a pound. All that weapon runs over $2 a pound. So there's no margin for error.
But you got a lot of country people come in here.
Most, 95% of our people are country people.
